newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 85-90 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 85-90 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 85 to 90 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
"I think the AGAs will show some healthy injections. There's been no weather," said one trader, noting favorable cash-to-futures spreads encouraged injections, particularly in the producing region.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged widely from 70 bcf to 110 bcf for the week ended September 13. The four-week average is 89 bcf.
Producing region stocks were at 57 percent of capacity in last week's report versus eastern stocks at 77 percent.
Last week, AGA showed overall storage rose by 98 bcf, well above expectations, but were still 325 bcf, or 13 percent, below the same year-ago period.

Last year at this time, total inventories gained 71 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would narrow the gap to last year to about 310 bcf. For the same week in 1995, eastern stocks rose by 46 bcf, while producing stocks were up by 18 bcf.
